articles.title: In 2024, Michigan Tech used treated waste glass to build stronger roads; a 6% mix raised stability by 42.3% and skid resistance by 38.6%
articles.summary: US News: In a road-building experiment, Michigan Tech researchers have uncovered a promising use for waste glass that would otherwise be discarded. In a study,.
articles.body: In a road-building experiment, Michigan Tech researchers have uncovered a promising use for waste glass that would otherwise be discarded. In a study, researchers tested asphalt mixed with surface-treated waste glass and found that a 6% blend delivered a 42.3% increase in dynamic stability compared with a conventional mixture. That same blend also improved anti-skid performance by 38.6%, giving it the strongest friction result among all the glass contents tested. To achieve this, the team treated the glass with APTES, a silane coupling agent that helped it bond more effectively with the asphalt. The findings point to a genuine role for recycled glass in building stronger, safer road surfaces.How was waste glass treated for asphaltAccording to the study published in ScienceDirect, titled ‘Performance evaluation of surface treatment waste glass as aggregate in asphalt mixture’, the team compared two approaches: physical abrasion and chemical surface treatment. For the chemical route, they used 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane, or APTES, a silane coupling agent designed to improve how well the glass and asphalt interact. Glass was immersed in an APTES mixture, then cured at a range of temperatures. Afterwards, the researchers examined the treated material using microscopy, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, boiling tests and contact-angle measurements.The treatment clearly made the asphalt adhere more strongly to the glass. According to the study, chemically treated samples outperformed those that underwent only physical abrasion, with APTES-treated glass showing adhesion rates above 90% across every curing temperature tested. Curing at 160°C produced the strongest adhesion work of all. The researchers concluded that silane treatment effectively bridges the gap between inorganic glass and organic asphalt, strengthening the bond at their interface.Why did 6% treated glass improve skid resistanceTo gauge how the mixtures held up under repeated loading at high temperatures, the team assessed dynamic stability. Compared with mixtures containing 6%, 8% and 10% surface-treated waste glass, tests were run at 60°C and dynamic stability was measured in cycles per millimetre. The conventional mixture recorded 4,158 cycles per millimetre. At 6% treated glass, dynamic stability rose by 42.3%. The gain was even larger at 8%, reaching 54.2%, and it recorded 6,412 cycles per millimetre, though at 10%, the improvement fell away sharply to just 3.1%. The researchers put this down to the treated glass strengthening the bond between aggregate and asphalt, producing a more compact, interlocking structure.That 6% mixture also stood out in skid resistance testing. Using a tyre-road dynamic friction testing system, the team measured the friction coefficient of specimens containing varying amounts of treated waste glass, against a conventional-mixture baseline of 0.44. At 6% treated glass, the friction coefficient increased by 38.6%; at 8% the gain narrowed to 29.5%, and at 10% it fell further to 18.2%. With a recorded friction coefficient of 0.61, the 6% mixture was identified as the optimal result for skid resistance, a result the researchers attributed partly to the larger frictional contact area the treated glass provided, along with stronger cohesion between glass and asphalt.What made 6% treated glass the optimal mixThe results suggest the most effective mixture wasn't simply the one with the most recycled glass. Although 8% gave the highest dynamic stability, the 6% mixture held up strongly across several measures, including the best low-temperature performance; the small-beam specimens at that content reached their highest low-temperature indicators. As the Michigan Tech record puts it: "incorporating surface-treated waste glass at an optimal proportion of 6% within the asphalt mixture led to a 42.3% increase in dynamic stability and a 38.6% enhancement in anti-skid performance compared to standard mixtures." The original study recommends APTES coating with a 6% waste-glass content by total aggregate weight; the researchers caution that long-term performance, including durability, environmental effects and cost, still needs further investigation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: California officers found 194 abandoned Dungeness crab traps off two rivers; violations wasted hundreds of crabs and brought four-year permit suspensions
articles.summary: US News: Two commercial fishermen have had their licences suspended and vessel permits revoked for four years after wildlife officers recovered 194 abandoned D.
articles.body: Two commercial fishermen have had their licences suspended and vessel permits revoked for four years after wildlife officers recovered 194 abandoned Dungeness crab traps from waters off the Del Norte County coast. The enforcement action, finalised during an August meeting of the California Fish and Game Commission, involved 66-year-old Darryl Donovan of Gilroy and 60-year-old Terry Groat of Crescent City. The two men were investigated over abandoned commercial fishing gear found in Northern California waters during two consecutive fishing seasons. According to reporting by Patch, state wildlife officials recommended the penalties after finding serious violations. The abandoned equipment had resulted in hundreds of Dungeness crabs being wasted and also created entanglement risks for marine wildlife. The investigation involved joint air and sea patrols carried out by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife's Marine Enforcement District and crews from the United States Coast Guard Air Station Humboldt Bay.Patrols find hundreds of abandoned trapsThe first investigation focused on waters near the mouth of the Klamath River after the 2023-24 commercial Dungeness crab season ended. Aerial and marine patrols spotted dozens of buoys that appeared to have been left unattended offshore. Wildlife officers then carried out a recovery operation to locate and remove the traps beneath the water. State investigators connected at least 107 abandoned traps to Donovan. Inspection records showed that the equipment had been left in the water beyond the legal period for servicing. California fishing rules require commercial crabbers to service active traps at least once every 96 hours. The requirement is designed to reduce the death of crabs caught in the traps and limit the loss of fishing equipment. Investigators cited Donovan for several violations. These included failing to service traps within the required 96-hour period, failing to file mandatory fishing activity reports and using buoys that were not properly tagged or marked. A second investigation began after the 2024-25 commercial crab season. Wildlife officers examined several strings of submerged fishing gear found near the mouth of the Smith River. Officers recovered 87 abandoned traps linked to Groat. The allegations against Groat were similar to those against Donovan. They included failing to service traps, using untagged buoys, failing to submit required reports and allowing hundreds of Dungeness crabs to die inside the abandoned equipment.Ghost gear continues to catch marine lifeThe case has drawn attention to the environmental risks created by abandoned commercial fishing equipment, often known as ghost gear. When crab traps are left in the sea, they can continue catching marine animals even when no fishermen are checking them. This process is known as ghost fishing. Crabs and fish can enter the traps and become trapped. They may eventually die from starvation or stress. Their bodies can then attract other animals, which may enter the same traps and become trapped themselves. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife has warned that abandoned traps and their lines can create risks for marine animals beyond the target crab species. Lines attached to unattended buoys can become entanglement hazards for animals moving through coastal waters. Species at risk include humpback whales, blue whales and Pacific leatherback sea turtles. Lost fishing gear can also affect other commercial fishermen. Lines and equipment left in the water can create navigation problems for vessels operating in the same areas. Wildlife entanglements can also lead authorities to shorten fishing seasons as they try to reduce risks to marine mammals and other protected species. That can create financial problems for commercial operators who follow the rules and depend on the fishery for their livelihoods. California's 840-mile coastline is regularly patrolled by wildlife officers who enforce state environmental and fisheries laws.Commission imposes four-year vessel penaltiesAfter state wildlife prosecutors submitted their recommendations, the California Fish and Game Commission considered the cases during its two-day meeting on August 12 and 13. The commission suspended the personal commercial fishing licences of both Donovan and Groat for two years. The men also received four-year suspensions of the Dungeness crab vessel permits connected to their operations. The vessel restrictions prevent the affected commercial boats from taking part in the fishery through 2030. The penalties cover both the individual licences and the vessel permits, making the enforcement action significantly longer for the fishing operations themselves. State officials said enforcement of fishing gear and trap recovery rules is important for protecting marine resources and reducing the environmental damage caused by abandoned equipment. The rules are also intended to protect commercial fishermen who comply with regulations and depend on healthy crab populations and safe fishing grounds. The recovery of 194 traps across the two investigations shows the scale of the problem facing Northern California waters. By removing abandoned gear and penalising operators accused of leaving it behind, state authorities are seeking to reduce continued ghost fishing and the wider risks that lost commercial equipment creates for marine life and other vessels along the Pacific coast.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1976, Tokelau’s Easter festival began as a small sports day; 50 years later its founder returned with four generations of family
articles.summary: Rest of World News: What began as a small community sports gathering in 1976 has grown into one of the most important celebrations for Tokelauans in Aotearoa New Zealand..
articles.body: What began as a small community sports gathering in 1976 has grown into one of the most important celebrations for Tokelauans in Aotearoa New Zealand. The Tokelau Easter Festival now brings together communities from New Zealand, Australia, Hawai‘i and the three atolls of Tokelau for several days of sport, culture, faith and family. Fifty years after the first tournament, the festival reached a particularly personal milestone in 2026, founder Ioane Iosua returned to experience it alongside four generations of his family. According to the festival’s organiser, Mafutaga Tupulaga Tokelau i Aukilani (MTTA), the 50th-anniversary gathering represented not simply five decades of sport, but a continuing connection between Tokelauan families and generations.How a small Tokelauan sports gathering began in 1976The roots of the festival can be traced to Ioane Iosua’s efforts to bring Tokelauan young people together through sport. According to MTTA’s founding history, Iosua and his cousins first became involved in rugby league after walking to a nearby club and asking to play. He eventually formed an Auckland team and connected with family in Porirua, leading to regional Tokelau rugby matches.The games quickly became about more than what happened on the field. Whether the team won or lost, the gatherings ended with families sharing food, singing and dancing fatele, a traditional Tokelauan performance. The matches became an annual event alternating between Auckland and Porirua before expanding to other communities including Rotorua, Taupō, Manawatū and Hutt Valley. Other sports were eventually added as the gathering grew.That early combination of competition and community laid the foundation for what would become the Tokelau Easter Festival. The 1976 event was the beginning of a tradition that has continued for five decades, growing from a humble sports day into a major Tokelauan cultural gathering.The Easter tournament grew into a four-day celebrationBy 2026, the event had become far broader than the rugby matches that helped start it. The 50th-anniversary Tokelau Easter Festival was held at Bruce Pulman Park in Takanini, Auckland, from April 3 to 6, bringing together Tokelauan communities from across Aotearoa New Zealand, Australia, Hawai‘i and Tokelau itself. It is the largest gathering of the Tokelauan diaspora in the world.Sport remains at the heart of the celebration, but the modern tournament features a wide range of competitions. The 2026 programme included tag rugby, netball, basketball, kilikiti, rugby league and volleyball, with divisions for children, teenagers and adults. This structure allows several generations of a family to participate at the same event rather than leaving the tournament solely to adult competitors.The festival also includes traditional dance, cultural activities, church services and educational and leadership programmes. The 2026 schedule included Po Fatele performances, a youth speech showcase, a multi-denominational church service and workshops covering subjects including artificial intelligence, recruitment, mental health and culture.Fifty years later, the founder returned with four generations of his familyThe 2026 festival carried a special significance for Iosua. It was the first time the founder experienced the Easter Festival with four generations of his family present. The moment connected the person who helped establish the gathering with descendants who were able to experience the tradition decades after its beginning.For Iosua, the festival's original purpose was always larger than sport. His vision was to share Tokelauan culture with the wider community while creating a cultural anchor for his family and the Tokelauan people. His founding story shows how sport became a practical way of bringing families together and maintaining those connections across different parts of New Zealand.The four-generation gathering therefore offered a striking picture of how far that original idea had travelled. A community activity started by young Tokelauans decades earlier had become an event in which children, parents, grandparents and great-grandparents could participate together.The festival became a way to keep Tokelauan culture connected across generationsThe significance of the Easter Festival extends beyond its sporting competitions. For a diaspora spread across different countries and communities, the gathering provides a regular opportunity for people to reconnect with relatives, meet other Tokelauan families and pass cultural traditions to younger generations. The festival is designed to strengthen bonds across generations while celebrating Tokelauan heritage.That purpose is visible in the structure of the modern event. Alongside competitive sport are traditional dance, cultural showcases, church activities and youth programmes. The festival's 2026 theme, “Raising Leaders, Rooted in Culture,” reflected the organisers' emphasis on giving younger Tokelauans opportunities to develop while remaining connected to their heritage.The tournament has also continued to expand geographically. What began with connections between Auckland and Porirua eventually incorporated communities across New Zealand and international participants from places including Australia, Hawai‘i and Tokelau. The result is a gathering that brings together a Tokelauan community much larger than the original group that played those early matches.A 1976 sports day became a 50-year family traditionThe history of the Tokelau Easter Festival is ultimately a story about how a simple community activity can acquire meaning across generations. In 1976, the idea was to bring Tokelauans together through sport. Over the following decades, the matches became annual gatherings where people also shared food, music, dance and family connections.Half a century later, the same tradition had become a four-day celebration involving multiple sports, cultural performances, faith and education. And at its 50th anniversary, the man who helped start it was there with four generations of his family.For MTTA, the milestone is a celebration of Tokelauan unity and resilience. For Iosua's family, it was also a rare chance to see the legacy of an idea that began with a few rugby players continuing into a fourth generation, with sport still providing the connection that brought everyone together in the first place.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump’s ‘deepest, darkest China’ gets a Brics sequel with Iran's cameo as India walks tightrope
articles.summary: India News: What could be a fresh diplomatic headache for Donald Trump? A picture of Prime Minister Narendra Modi holding hands with Iranian President Masoud Peze.
articles.body: What could be a fresh diplomatic headache for Donald Trump? A picture of Prime Minister Narendra Modi holding hands with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with Russian President Vladimir Putin standing alongside them at the Brics Summit, has brought together three countries whose ties with Washington range from strategic competition to open confrontation.The image also echoes a remark Trump made last year after PM Modi, Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping were pictured together at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit. “Looks like we’ve lost India and Russia to deepest, darkest, China. May they have a long and prosperous future together!” Trump had said.This time, Iran, one of Washington’s most adversarial rivals, has joined the picture, adding another layer to the geopolitical message from a grouping that Trump has repeatedly viewed with suspicion. The US president has not yet commented on the Brics summit.Trump pressure on BricsUS President Donald Trump has repeatedly warned Brics against challenging the dominance of the US dollar, putting the grouping’s push for greater use of local currencies at the centre of tensions with Washington. In November 2024, Trump threatened 100% tariffs on Brics countries if they backed another currency to replace the dollar.“We require a commitment from these Countries that they will neither create a new Brics Currency, nor back any other currency to replace the mighty US Dollar or, they will face 100% Tariffs, and should expect to say goodbye to selling into the wonderful US economy,” Trump said in a post on Truth Social.Trump has also dismissed the prospect of Brics replacing the dollar in global trade, saying there was “no chance” of that happening and warning that countries attempting to do so should “wave goodbye to America”.The issue remains central to Brics’ economic agenda, although the grouping has increasingly focused on making trade and payments in national currencies easier rather than creating a common currency. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, speaking at the Brics Business Forum, called for greater use of national currencies among members, along with mechanisms to manage currency risks and facilitate reciprocal settlements.“One of the most important steps is to expand the use of national currencies in trade among the members. This step must be accompanied by the establishment of the necessary instruments for managing currency risks and reciprocal settlements,” Pezeshkian said.He also argued that the existing financial system was vulnerable because of its concentration around a limited number of currencies and called for the New Development Bank to play a bigger role in financing infrastructure and energy projects through local currencies and other mechanisms.Putin, meanwhile, did not directly mention replacing the dollar at this year’s forum. Instead, he described a broader shift in the global economic order, with emerging economies becoming increasingly important.“Right now, the world is undergoing structural, deep, profound shifts. It is explained by the fact that the so-called old leaders which used to be the vanguard of economic growth in the second half of the 20th century, are being replaced by new engines of growth. When I say old, this is just a formality - all of us understand what we are talking about,” he said.For Washington, the concern is not simply whether Brics creates a new currency, but whether a larger share of global trade and financial transactions gradually moves away from the dollar.India walks a tight ropeFor India, the Brics summit comes at a sensitive point in its economic relationship with the US. The India-US trade deal is “more or less” finalised, with the two sides working on a framework for preferential market access before signing it at an appropriate time. A few issues remain under discussion.The talks come as Trump continues to step up pressure on India over its purchase of Russian oil. In 2025, he had warned of further tariff action and later imposed 50% tariffs on Indian goods, adding to the economic stakes for New Delhi as it seeks to deepen trade with the US.India is meanwhile pursuing multiple trade agreements to widen market access. It has signed nine trade agreements over the past five years covering economies with a combined GDP of $60 trillion, while talks with Chile are at an advanced stage and New Zealand has been targeted for an early rollout.The balancing act is also reflected in India’s broader trade priorities. Its total exports reached $863 billion in 2025-26, including $421 billion in services, with the government seeking to diversify services exports beyond IT and professional services and expand areas such as fintech and digital services.The conflict involving Iran and the disruption around the Strait of Hormuz have added another layer to the equation. The waterway is a crucial route for global oil shipments, making stability in the Gulf directly relevant to India’s energy security, trade and the safety of Indian seafarers.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: San Jose woman arrested after video accusing father of trafficking his 6-year-old daughter goes viral
articles.summary: US News: A San Jose woman who went viral after accusing a father of sex-trafficking his own 6-year-old daughter because he is a man of color and the girl appea.
articles.body: A San Jose woman who went viral after accusing a father of sex-trafficking his own 6-year-old daughter because he is a man of color and the girl appears white has been arrested on suspicion of stalking and hate crimes, police said.The woman, 47, was arrested Thursday after San Jose police investigated a series of incidents involving her, including the confrontation with the father and his daughter in the city's Almaden neighborhood on September 6. Investigators said she had approached the pair multiple times and made discriminatory remarks.The original encounter was captured on video by the father who posted it on TikTok. In the footage, the woman can be heard telling him she believed he was trafficking the child because the girl looked white while he was a “man of color.”“I believe you're either buying or selling or trafficking this child,” she said in the video.The woman also claimed she worked with federal authorities. “I'm recording you too,” she told the father before saying she was checking that he was not sex-trafficking the girl because she allegedly did not look like his child.The father had described himself online as “brown” and said his daughter is half-white. The incident happened while he was walking with the girl near a small park in the Almaden neighborhood.Woman allegedly involved in other incidentsThe September 6 confrontation was not the only incident that drew police attention.According to police, investigators learned during their inquiry that the woman was allegedly responsible for a series of other incidents. One occurred at a South San Jose high school three days after the confrontation with the father and daughter.Police said they used automated license plate reader technology to identify the woman's vehicle and then conducted a broader investigation through the San Jose Police Department's assaults unit.She was ultimately booked into Santa Clara County Main Jail on suspicion of stalking, hate crimes and other offences.The arrest came just days after the video of the confrontation went viral, drawing widespread criticism over the woman's decision to infer that the child was being trafficked based on the different appearances of the father and daughter.The father, who has asked to remain anonymous, told KRON he was walking while his daughter was a little ahead of him riding her bike. As the daughter stopped to wait for him to catch up, he said the woman, who they had never seen before, stopped her car near the daughter for a few seconds and then drove up to him. “Are you buying or selling today?” she asked him.“I was already uncomfortable because she had approached my daughter, so I was taken aback,” the father said. “She asked me the same question again and then drove away, turning onto another neighborhood street.”The father headed in the other direction with his daughter after the hateful comments but said that the woman came around from behind them. “She slowed down and said something to the effect of asking whether I was even legal in the country,” he said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
